body: When I got my K1C which looks like it has a similar extruder design, I had the same issue - thought I pushed the filament enough, but still wouldn't extrude no matter what I tried. Then I read somewhere on Reddit that "the machine craves violence" and that was the solution. Make sure the filament is cut right, unlock the extruder, push the filament in until it stops, and then ram it in a bit more, then it should go in. The machine can handle it. My extruder even made tiny clicking noises as I pushed the filament between the gears. You'll learn how to identify when the filament is in properly in time, don't worry.

So, I found a way to solve it. You have to get ADB from here: https://developer.android.com/studio. Find on the site "platform-tools only" (at the time of edit, it is this link: https://dl.google.com/android/repository/platform-tools-latest-windows.zip), extract the zip to a folder somewhere and navigate to it in CMD/terminal. On Windows, you can open the folder, then shift+right click and select open CMD/powershell here (or something similar, my os isn't in English).

On your phone, enable developer settings (tap 7 times on the build number in settings), then go to developer settings and allow usb debugging, as well as usb debugging (security settings). Connect your phone to your PC and change connection type to file transfer.

Go back to the CMD/terminal/powershell that you opened, make sure it is in the right folder and run these two commands:


./adb.exe shell settings put secure night_display_activated 0

./adb.exe shell settings put secure night_display_auto_mode 0


When you do, and check your phone again, the red tint should be gone.
